Ready for the maintainer to merge.

The MCP post description names the plasma post. The new tests cover the workflow, undo and redo, named refusals, and the post block for incorrect cut order. The guide explains the limits of plasma verification. The change meets issue #1871.

Local checks used the PR head merged with upstream/main at `8719d8b7a028f0c93cc78fe32ccbfdf5297a0dca`. The trial merge had no conflicts. All commands ran locally in the foreground.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --no-run`: passed.
- `mcp_plasma`: 4 passed.
- `mcp`: 22 passed.
- `mcp_coolant`: 5 passed.
- `mcp_setup_mount_trace`: 3 passed.
- `mcp_holder`: 5 passed.
- `sinker_electrode_mcp`: 2 passed.
- `mcp_wire_contour`: 5 passed.
- `mcp_pockets`: 3 passed.
- `mcp_pick`: 7 passed.
- Total: 56 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `git diff --check upstream/main`: passed.

The quick-gate plan included unrelated changes from main because the trial merge was not committed. I used the module map to select the MCP suites listed above instead of running that broad plan.

Safety scope: the production change is one description string. G-code generation, gouge and collision checks, stock simulation, and geometry code are unchanged. Mutation tests were not required or run. No goldens changed. No UI files changed, so screenshots are not required.

Process check: the PR body has `Process change: yes`. The process rule in both the PR base and current upstream assigns the version increment to the merge session. This PR correctly leaves `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` unchanged.

Requested changes: none.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
